History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
40-year-old woman with 3-week history of left-sided hearing loss and facial numbness; possible Bell’s palsy—GP clinic assessment arranged today.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Progressive reduction in hearing on the left side with numbness of the left peri-auricular face/jaw for ~3 weeks.  
• Course: Persistent; numbness “all the time,” hearing subjectively reduced throughout period.  
• Associated symptoms: Intermittent left-sided tinnitus; occasional dizziness coinciding with tinnitus.  
• Denies: Ear discharge, otalgia, pruritus, fever, dysphagia, dysarthria, limb weakness or numbness, visual change.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: None identified.  
• ROS otherwise unremarkable per transcript.

Past Medical History:
• Nasal polyps – intermittent flares managed with intranasal spray (name unknown).  
• Remote history of labyrinthitis (no current symptoms).  
• No other chronic illnesses reported.

Medications:
• Intranasal spray for nasal polyps – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Rennie (antacid) PRN – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• No regular prescription medications otherwise.

Allergies:
• Latex – reaction not described.

Social History:
• Occupation: Professional jockey (horse racing).  
• Impact: Reduced training due to dizziness/hearing issues.  
• Living situation: Initially stated lives alone, then clarified lives with partner (conflict noted).  
• Pets: None.  
• Smoking, alcohol, recreational drugs: Not discussed.

Family History:
• Brother: Neurofibromatosis.  
• Otherwise non-contributory per patient.

Physical Examination:
(Not performed – video consult only.)

Investigations:
None in this consult.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Left-sided hearing loss, facial numbness, possible Bell’s palsy  
  • Assessment: Unilateral facial sensory change and auditory symptoms; Bell’s palsy considered most likely among differentials (others include otitis media, acoustic pathology, central lesion).  
  • Plan:  
    – Same-day face-to-face GP clinic appointment for full neurological and otoscopic examination.  
    – Confirm or refute Bell’s palsy; initiate standard treatment (e.g., steroids ± antivirals) if confirmed.  
    – Consider audiometry and referral to ENT/neuro as indicated.

Issue 2: Patient anxiety about seriousness of condition  
  • Assessment: Patient expresses fear of life-threatening illness.  
  • Plan: Reassured that current presentation unlikely life-threatening; further reassurance to be provided after physical exam.

General plan items:  
• Admin team to contact patient and arrange central London clinic slot today; patient to phone support line in 5 minutes to confirm.  
• Safety-net advice: Attend ED if new weakness, severe headache, vision change, worsening dizziness, or other concerning symptoms.  
• Documentation of face-to-face findings and follow-up plan after examination.

Quality checks:
• Missing expected elements: No vital signs; no physical exam; full medication and allergy details incomplete; smoking/alcohol history not obtained.  
• Internal conflicts: Patient first stated she lives alone, later said she lives with her partner—conflict noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear audio; minimal background noise; no major inaudible sections.
